quotes.text: I want to suggest that to write to your best abilities, it behooves you to construct your own toolbox and then build up enough muscle so you can carry it with you. Then, instead of looking at a hard job and getting discouraged, you will perhaps seize the correct tool and get immediately to work.

We suggest that the capabilities of AI create a 'jagged technological frontier' where some tasks are easily done by AI, while others, though seemingly similar in difficulty level, are outside the current capability of AI.
quotes.attribution: Dell'Acqua et al. 2023, Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier

quotes.text: We find that 57% of the analysed questions in the Virology subset contain errors.
quotes.attribution: Gema et al. 2024, on Errors in MMLU

quotes.text: We are all plagued by failures—by missed subtleties, overlooked knowledge, and outright errors.
By the end of this year, the least important thing you will be able to do with frontier AI systems will be getting chatbots to answer questions.
quotes.attribution: Dean W. Ball, Among the Agents, 9 Jan 2026

terms.definition: An AI model trained on vast text data to generate and understand language — the core technology behind ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini
The concept that AI capabilities are uneven — some seemingly hard tasks are easy for AI while some seemingly easy tasks are impossible
When an AI model generates plausible-sounding but incorrect information, particularly fabricated references and links
Workflows built around AI model outputs using traditional computing — combining model intelligence with tools like search and code
The raw AI intelligence that outputs sequences of tokens, distinct from the orchestration layer that wraps it
The ability of AI models to work across different types of input and output — text, images, audio, video
A tool within AI chatbots that allows the model to write and execute computer code to solve problems
AI-powered multi-step research tools that search, synthesise, and report on topics with citations
A structured approach to skill development involving reflection and targeted repetition
Cognition framework describing levels of learning engagement: Interactive, Constructive, Active, Passive
